Plan: export a region of a file (issue #18)¶

Branch: 18-region-export, from main at 8896568, rebased on 2c3c7cd (after the GPU merge, PR #20). Status: steps 1–9 implemented (2026-10-20), PR #22. The user tested the GUI on screen (2026-10-20).

1. Goal¶

Issue #18 asks for these items:

  1. Export a smaller part of a data file to a new file.

  2. A new panel (window) where the user sets the time (or sample) range and the frequency range of the export.

  3. Two ways to fill the panel:

    • from the current channel setup;

    • from a selection on the waterfall: right-click the waterfall, choose an export mode, and drag a box with a crosshair cursor.

  4. The values go into the panel, and the user checks them before the file is written.

3. Design decisions¶

Topic

Decision

Reason

What is exported

A time range [t0, t1) and, optionally, a frequency band [f_lo, f_hi].

The issue asks for time / sample and frequency.

Full band (no frequency selection)

Copy the raw bytes of the sample range unchanged: same sample format, same rate, same center frequency. The header is not copied.

Lossless and fast. This is the common “cut a piece out of a big file” case.

Frequency band selected

Mix the band center down to 0 Hz, low-pass filter, and decimate. The output center frequency is fc + band center. The output rate is fs / D.

A smaller file at a lower rate. This is what “frequency range” means for IQ data.

Filter for the export

The band is the passband. A transition band of 25 % of the bandwidth on each side. D = max(1, ⌊fs / (1.25 · BW)⌋), so the transition band does not alias into the passband. Blackman windowed sinc with N ≈ 5.5 · fs / (0.25 · BW) taps (cutoff in the middle of the transition band).

The demod filter (taps ≈ 12 · fs / BW, cutoff at BW / 2) attenuates the band edges by 6 dB. An export must keep the whole selected band. The Blackman window gives about 74 dB of stopband.

Cost of narrow bands

No limit on the number of taps. The FIR computes only the kept outputs, so the work per input sample is N / D ≈ 27 multiply-adds for any bandwidth.

A narrow band in a wide file (20 MS/s to 10 kHz: D = 1600, N ≈ 44 000) costs the same per input sample as a wide band.

Output rate

fs / D, an integer decimation. The window shows the exact rate.

A rational resampler to a chosen rate is more work. It can come later if needed.

Output format

Full band: the source format. Band selected: cf32 (default) or ci16. With ci16 the export scales by 32768 and counts clipped samples (WARN).

The filter output is float. ci16 halves the size.

File type

SigMF (default) or raw, as for recordings. A raw name carries the rate and frequency, so wvt can open it with no options.

Same as the recorder.

Metadata (SigMF)

core:sample_rate, core:datatype, core:frequency (in the capture), core:datetime = the source start time + t0 when the source SigMF has one, core:description. A wvt:extract object with the source file name, sample range, band, D, taps and filter.

The export can be traced back to its source.

Source annotations

Not copied (the reader does not parse them).

Can come later with the SigMF reader work.

Writer

Reuse Recorder through a SampleRing, as FileGenJob does. Add RecordConfig::exactPath: the user’s file name instead of PREFIX_<date>_….

One SigMF writer. exactPath keeps the user’s name.

Range limits

Time inside the loaded segment (#16). Band inside fc ± fs / 2. BW at least fs / 100 000 (D at most 80 000).

Same limits as the rest of the view.

Background job

ExtractJob (src/dsp/extract.*): its own thread, chunks of about 4 M input samples, progress, cancel. Cancel deletes the partial files. An existing file is not overwritten unless the user confirms.

A cancelled export is not a usable file.

Disk space

Before starting, check the free space (statvfs) against the size estimate. Too little: an error, nothing is written.

Large exports can fill a disk.

GPU (#3, PR #20)

The export filter is CPU code in src/dsp/extract.cpp. When #20 is merged, it can use ChanJob / gpuChannelize.

#20 is not merged yet; #18 must not wait for it.

Logging (#14)

INFO at start (source, range, band, D, taps, output) and at the end (file, size, time). WARN for clipping and for clamped values. ERROR for failures, once, by the code that shows them.

docs/design/verbose-logging-plan.md.

The export window¶

Opened from a new Export button in toolbar row 1 (next to Audio), with Ctrl+E, or from the waterfall menu.

Row

Contents

Time

Start / End in seconds, or in samples (switch). The length and the sample count.

Band

Full band checkbox. When off: Low / High, or Center / BW (switch). Absolute frequency, or relative to fc with Rel. freq.

Fill from

View · Channel (offset and BW; time = the view) · Markers (T1 / T2, F1 / F2) · Select on waterfall

Output

Format (source / cf32 / ci16), SigMF / raw, path, as a text field (default: next to the source file, <name>_<t0>s_<fc>_<rate>).

Result

Output rate, D, taps, number of samples, file size, estimated time. Errors in red (for example “the band is outside the capture”).

Actions

Export, then a progress bar, Cancel, and the result line with the path.

The selection on the waterfall¶

  • Right-click (press and release without moving) on the waterfall opens a wvt menu:

    • Select a region to export…: crosshair mode;

    • Export this view: fill the window with the view (time and full band);

    • Export the channel: fill it from the channel.

  • Right-drag keeps the box zoom. The waterfall gets ImPlotFlags_NoMenus. ImPlot’s own menu then no longer opens on the waterfall: it has only axis settings, which the toolbar and double-click already give.

  • Crosshair mode: the cursor is a crosshair. A left-drag draws the box, and panning is off until the mouse is released. Esc cancels. The box fills Start / End / Low / High and opens the export window.

  • While the export window is open, the region shows as a draggable rectangle (ImPlot::DragRect) on the waterfall. Its edges and the panel values stay in step. The time range also shows as a shaded band on the I/Q, AM, FM and PM plots.

Command line¶

--extract-out PATH --extract T0:T1 [--extract-band LO:HI] [--extract-format cf32|ci16] [--record-format sigmf|raw]. Headless, with exit status 0 on success. --segment limits it the same way as in the window. It is for tests and scripts.

4. Implementation steps¶

  1. Extraction core (src/dsp/extract.h, src/dsp/extract.cpp).

    • ExtractConfig (source, sample range, band, format, file type, path) and ExtractPlan (D, taps, cutoff, output rate, sample count, bytes, or the error).

    • planExtract(cfg): all the checks of §3, and no I/O, so the window can call it every frame.

    • Full band: chunked byte copy. Band: chunked mix + FIR + decimate with the phase from the absolute index (each chunk reads its own input with the filter overlap, as processRange does).

    • Output through Recorder with exactPath. wvt:extract metadata.

  2. Recorder (src/io/recorder.*): RecordConfig::exactPath and the start datetime from the source.

  3. Background job: ExtractJob (progress, cancel deletes the files, status) and the disk-space check.

  4. Command line: --extract-out, --extract, --extract-band, --extract-format, and the usage text.

  5. Self-test tools/extract_check.cpp (§5).

  6. Export window (src/app/app_export.cpp): the window of §3, Export button, Ctrl+E, the “Fill from” buttons, progress, the result.

  7. Waterfall: NoMenus, the right-click menu, crosshair mode, the DragRect and the time bands on the right-hand plots.

  8. Source start time: guessMeta also reads core:datetime of the first capture, for the exported core:datetime.

  9. README: the window, the waterfall menu, the options, the file table.

5. Testing¶

Test

Check

extract_check: full band

A cf32 / ci16 / cu8 file with a header: the output bytes are exactly the source bytes of the range. The SigMF metadata has the same rate, format and frequency.

extract_check: band

Two tones, one inside and one outside the band. Out: the inside tone at f - band center, level within 0.1 dB. The outside tone at least 70 dB down. Rate fs / D.

extract_check: edges of the band

Tones at 0 %, 50 % and 100 % of the band: all within 0.1 dB.

extract_check: chunks

One export in one chunk and in many chunks: the same samples.

extract_check: checks

Band outside the capture, end before start, range outside the segment, too narrow: an error, no file.

extract_check: ci16

Scaling and the clip count.

extract_check: cancel

The partial files are deleted.

Headless

wvt FILE --extract 1:2 --extract-band 100.2M:100.4M --extract-out x writes the file. wvt opens it, and the tone shows at the right frequency.

GUI (you must do this)

The window, each “Fill from” button, the right-click menu, right-drag still zooms, crosshair mode, Esc, the rectangle and its edges, progress and Cancel, the overwrite question, an export of a 7 GB file.

Regression

All self-tests pass. Without the new options, the output and the log are the same as main.

6. Decisions needed¶

  1. Full band exports copy the bytes unchanged. Do you agree, or should the output always be one format (for example cf32)?

  2. Output rate: integer decimation only (rate fs / D), or also an exact rate that you type (needs a rational resampler)?

  3. Filter: passband = the selected band and a 25 % transition band (larger file, flat band). Or the demod filter (smaller file, edges 6 dB down)?

  4. Right-click on the waterfall: replace ImPlot’s own menu there with the wvt menu, and keep right-drag for the box zoom?

  5. Cancel deletes the partial file. Agreed?

  6. GPU: CPU first, and the GPU after #20 is merged?

  7. Range: inside the loaded segment only, or anywhere in the file?

7. Decisions (2026-10-20)¶

The user said to go with the recommendations:

  1. Full band: the bytes are copied unchanged.

  2. Output rate: integer decimation only (fs / D).

  3. Filter: the band is the passband, with a 25 % transition band.

  4. Right-click on the waterfall: wvt’s menu replaces ImPlot’s; right-drag keeps the box zoom.

  5. Cancel deletes the partial file.

  6. GPU: #20 is merged, so the export uses ChanJob / gpuChannelize from the start, with channelizeCpu as the fallback.

  7. Range: inside the loaded segment only.

Differences from the plan¶

  • Filter length: N = ⌈5.5 · fs / (0.25 · BW)⌉ | 1 and cutoff 0.625 · BW / fs, as planned. In the test, the band edges are 0.002 dB down and a tone outside the band is 92.8 dB down.

  • Full band, big-endian or swapped I/Q: the copy puts the bytes in the standard order (byte and I/Q swaps only), because the SigMF and raw names describe little-endian data in I/Q order.

  • No source start time: the export leaves out core:datetime instead of writing the time of the export.

  • Crosshair: the X11 layer does not change the system cursor, so selection mode draws a crosshair and a hint inside the waterfall.

  • The region box: ImPlot’s DragRect moves the whole box when you drag inside it, so the view does not pan inside the box while the export window is open. Pan outside it.

  • --export-window: opens the window at start (the --chan band, or the view). It is used for the screenshots below.

  • Default name: <source name>_<t0>s_<fc>MHz_<rate>Sps. The rate and frequency already in the source name are removed, because guessMeta takes the first match.

  • Window position: on the right, left of the audio window when that is open.

Verification (macOS)¶

  • The build has no warnings. extract_check (36 checks), gpu_check, segment_check, siggen_check, audio_check and log_check pass.

  • --help differs from main only by the new lines. A signal-generator file (--gen-out) has the same data as main, and the same metadata apart from core:datetime.

  • Headless: iqgen capture, --extract 0.5:1.5 --extract-band 100.25M:100.35M gives 125 000 samples at 125 kS/s, 100.3 MHz; an NFM WAV export of that file plays the tone. A second export to the same name fails with status 2.

  • Screenshots (Xvfb in a container, --export-window): the window with the view (full band, the two time lines on the waterfall) and with --chan 300k:150k (band 100.225–100.375 MHz, 200 kS/s, 295 taps, decimation 10, the box on the waterfall).
